stories.title: The Royal Observatory, Greenwich, founded in 1675
stories.summary: Royal Museums Greenwich says the Royal Observatory, Britain's oldest purpose-built scientific institution, was founded in 1675 and is the home of Greenwich Mean Time and the Prime Meridian. The foundation stone was laid on 10 August 1675.

cards.title: Royal Observatory Greenwich
cards.body: The official Royal Museums Greenwich history page says the Royal Observatory is Britain's oldest purpose-built scientific institution, founded in 1675, the birthplace of modern astronomy, and the home of Greenwich Mean Time and the Prime Meridian. It quotes Charles II's order to build a small observatory in Greenwich Park, notes that Christopher Wren was tasked with the design, and says Astronomer Royal John Flamsteed laid the foundation stone at 3.14pm on 10 August 1675 and moved in on 10 July 1676. In 1953 the Greenwich site became part of the National Maritime Museum. The page, read 21 November 2026, also says the site is temporarily closed for a capital project expected to reopen in spring 2028.
cards.why: The official home of the Prime Meridian, a natural pin for a globe.

stories.title: NOAA's Mauna Loa Baseline Observatory
stories.summary: NOAA's Global Monitoring Laboratory describes the Mauna Loa Observatory as an atmospheric research facility on the north flank of Mauna Loa, Hawai'i, continuously monitoring atmospheric change since the 1950s. Official coordinates and elevation are published on the observatory page.

location.name: Mauna Loa Baseline Observatory (NOAA-listed point)
location.note: Latitude 19.5362° N, longitude 155.5763° W, and elevation 3,397 metres are published on the official NOAA GML observatory page, read 21 Nov 2026. The same page says the 2022 Mauna Loa eruption cut off road access, and that a temporary access road was completed on 26 March 2026, with no general-public opening date yet established.

stories.script: NOAA's Global Monitoring Laboratory places the Mauna Loa Observatory on the north flank of Mauna Loa, at 3,397 metres, and says it has been continuously monitoring atmospheric change since the 1950s. Official NOAA pages say the observatory was constructed in 1956 and has run continuously since, and that Keeling CO2 measurements began in March 1958. Official NOAA pages distinguish the 1956 construction from the March 1958 Keeling record. The pin uses the observatory's published coordinates.

captions.text: NOAA has monitored the atmosphere here since the 1950s.
The pin uses NOAA's published coordinates.

cards.title: Mauna Loa Observatory
cards.body: The official NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory page says Mauna Loa Observatory sits on the north flank of Mauna Loa Volcano on the Island of Hawai'i, at an elevation of 3,397 metres (11,135 feet), and has been continuously monitoring and collecting data related to atmospheric change since the 1950s. It publishes the site coordinates as 19.5362° North, 155.5763° West. The page also states that the 2022 eruption of Mauna Loa cut off road access, that construction on a temporary access road was completed on 26 March 2026, and that no public opening date had yet been established when the page was read. NOAA's Global Monitoring Laboratory says the observatory was constructed in 1956 and has been continuously in operation since. A NOAA media release says Keeling CO2 measurements began in March 1958. These two official start statements are not collapsed into one day. The exact calendar day in March 1958 is [UNKNOWN] in this card.
cards.why: One of the world's primary climate-observing sites, with coordinates published by NOAA.

stories.title: CERN's Large Hadron Collider, started in 2008
stories.summary: CERN describes the Large Hadron Collider as the world's largest and most powerful particle accelerator: a 27-kilometre ring, about 100 metres underground on the Franco-Swiss border near Geneva. It first started up on 10 September 2008.

location.name: CERN, near Geneva (approx.)
location.note: Approximate pin for the CERN site on the Franco-Swiss border near Geneva. The LHC is a 27-kilometre ring, not a single building. A surveyed ring-point coordinate is [UNKNOWN] in this card.

stories.script: CERN describes the Large Hadron Collider as the world's largest and most powerful particle accelerator, a 27-kilometre ring about 100 metres underground on the Franco-Swiss border near Geneva. It first started up on 10 September 2008. The pin is approximate.

captions.text: The Large Hadron Collider, near Geneva.
CERN started the machine on 10 September 2008.

cards.title: Large Hadron Collider
cards.body: CERN's official LHC page says the collider is the world's largest and most powerful particle accelerator, a 27-kilometre ring of superconducting magnets that first started up on 10 September 2008, sitting in a tunnel 100 metres underground at CERN on the Franco-Swiss border near Geneva, Switzerland. The same page says the announcement of the discovery of the Higgs boson in July 2012 confirmed the mechanism predicted in 1964 through which fundamental particles acquire mass. CERN's official announcement of that observation is dated 4 July 2012.
cards.why: A flagship laboratory that can be flown to on a globe, cited from CERN.
